findings.title: Review could not be verified against the checked-out files
findings.description: Every tool call I made (Bash, Read, Grep) returned empty output, so I could not open `tick_status.py`, `store_context.py`, `session_days.py`, `tick_exit.py`, or `pyproject.toml`. The scope instructions require files to be read before a PASS, so I am not issuing one. The findings below come from the diff text alone. Please re-run the review once the tools return output.

findings.title: `_scope` reads all current units without bounding by the wanted range
findings.description: `_scope` calls `shape_units` for the whole shape, and `_product_status` calls `shape_units` again through `session_verdicts`, and a third time per product through `contract_lines`. Each call re-runs the same unit/request join, so the unit read happens twice per product. The result could be fetched once and passed down. This is a diff-only observation and I have not confirmed how large the unit table gets.

findings.title: `tick_status`/`tick_coverage` define the verbs with lazy imports and a module-level `assert`
findings.description: `_BUCKET_ROWS` is guarded by a bare `assert`, which is stripped under `python -O`, so the "report omits a bucket" check silently disappears in optimized runs. An explicit `raise` at import time would keep the guard in every mode. Separately, `build_status` in `tick_status_build.py` uses a list comprehension with `await` inside `tuple([...])`. It runs sequentially, which is fine, but a plain loop would read more clearly.

findings.title: Exception mapping for storage failures is sound in the diff
findings.description: `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses `TickPreflightError`, and `run_mapped` checks the `storage` tuple before calling `exit_code_for`, so the more specific exit code wins. The `except Exception` there is documented as a process-boundary handler and re-raises unmapped errors, which matches the project rule. I could not confirm that `exit_code_for` does not also map the subclass differently.
